identity: Television actor and singer · United States · 1922–1965
title: Dorothy Dandridge's birth chart
metaDescription: Dorothy Dandridge's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.5° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 13.9° Cancer, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 16.5° of Scorpio is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Jupiter in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 1.2° Scorpio; Venus stands at 9.3° Sagittarius; Mars stands at 7.0° Aquarius. The tradition reads thought steeped in tone and memory from Mercury, attraction declared rather than implied from Venus, effort aimed through strategy and words from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Venus and Uranus — a square holding at 0.4°. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Uranus trine Pluto at 1.4°, and the Sun square Neptune at 1.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: the Sun, Uranus, Pluto close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. The Moon in Cancer at 13.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Libra at 15.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 6 water, 2 fire, 2 air; by modality, 5 fixed, 3 cardinal, 2 mutable. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Venus, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.1° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 13.9°.
